title: Hiskalelus of the sefiros: bittul in the opposite, light in a vessel, and the essence turned by mesirus nefesh
overview:
Now comes what we have all been waiting for: how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are included in one another, down to *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma*. Each *sefira* divides into ten and ten into ten, the *sefira* and the *partzuf*; in the *etzem hamidda* itself a bias turns every point to its own side, like a bribed judge, and only as it spreads out can it compromise.

The first kind of *hiskalelus* is *bittul*: the prosecutor becomes the defender, sugar overpowers cocoa, the murderer's childhood becomes the reason to throw the book at him. It works because each side hides its opposite. The second kind is a light in a vessel, where the opposite strengthens: feeding your hungry enemy, the spy, the raise before the firing, the father who rebukes because he loves, the harsh cure. Like red ink spelling "green", light and vessel do not contradict, so both can come at once. In the simple points nothing combines, except through *mesirus nefesh*, which makes even sins into merits. From it come three ways of *avoda*: trust past the vessel, a light that overpowers, and enjoying the challenge itself.

terms.gloss: inclusion: one attribute included in another, from a nullification in it to working together with it
division: each sefira divided into ten, and each of those into ten again
the essence of the attribute: a bias that turns every point to its own side and has no recognizable division
nullification: here a thing totally turned over into its opposite, which it can be only because the opposite is hidden in it
gevura of chesed: as light in a vessel, kindness done in the garment of judgment, the strongest kindness
chesed of gevura: as light in a vessel, judgment done by way of kindness, the strongest judgment
matter and form: like ink and the word it spells, a light and its vessel do not contradict
a kind finds its kind and wakes up: a nullified thing returns when it meets its own kind
self-sacrifice: the soul's connection to G-d Himself, above the division of chesed and gevura
a returnee to Judaism, in whom even the essence of bad is turned to good

sections.title: Every sefira divides into ten and ten into ten, but in the essence a bias turns everything to its side
sections.summary: Before the kinds of *hiskalelus* (inclusion) can be explained, each *sefira* has to be divided into ten and each of those into ten again, the *sefira* and the *partzuf*. In the *etzem hamidda* (the essence of the attribute) there is no recognizable division, and like a bribe it turns every point to its own side; only once it spreads out can it compromise.

phrases.en: Now that we've explained everything

phrases.he: יש להבין בפרטי התכללות דעשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: We have to understand the particular types of interclusion, interrelationship, or *hiskalelus* between the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: **Now that we've explained everything**, from the *Atzmus Ein Sof* and the *reshimu* to *nekuda*, *sefira* and *partzuf*, comes what we have been waiting for: **the particular types of interclusion, interrelationship, or hiskalelus between the ten sefiros of Atzilus**. That is, what *chesed* of *gevura* means, up to *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*, as was said at the beginning of chapter 10.

phrases.en: but first

phrases.he: יש לבאר ענין פרטי התחלקות הספירות לי' וי' לי' כו'
phrases.en: First we have to understand how each *sefira* divides into ten, and each of those ten divides into ten further.

phrases.he: כמו חסד שבחכמה שנחלק גם הוא לי', וכהאי גוונא גבורה שבחכמה נחלק לי' כו'.

blocks.text: **First we have to understand how each sefira divides into ten, and each of those ten divides into ten further.** *Chachma* has *Keser* of *chachma*, *chachma* of *chachma*, *bina* of *chachma* and so on; then *chesed* of *chachma* has its own ten, as does *gevura* of *chachma*. You could divide forever, but usually we stop at a hundred.

We stop at a hundred because this chapter explains two main types of *hiskalelus*, and we count one division for each. It ties to chapter 20: *chachma* alone is like a *nekuda* (a point); divided into ten the first way, a *sefira*; divided again the second way, a *partzuf*. First a general explanation of ten into ten, then the two types.

phrases.en: because *chachma* includes ten *sefiros*, ten subdivisions.
For example, there's *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma*.

phrases.he: להטות כלפי זכות או כלפי חוב
phrases.en: you can have an intuitive intellect that leans towards merit or towards guilt.

blocks.text: **Because chachma includes ten sefiros**, such as **chesed and gevura of chachma**: **an intuitive intellect that leans towards merit or towards guilt**, *zechus* or *chov*.

blocks.title: My better judgment tells me
blocks.text: Asked whether something is a good idea, you may not be able to explain it in *bina*, but you have a feeling: "my better judgment tells me" it is not, or it just seems right. A judge too may feel, without knowing why, that a man is innocent or guilty. Those are *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma*.

phrases.en: Let's say we're talking of *chesed d'chachma*: the person thinks that he's innocent, he thinks that it's a good thing.
That itself also has ten.
for example, there's *chesed* and *gevura* of *chesed d'chachma*.

phrases.he: לזכות באופן כך וכך, ולחוב יחייב גם הוא באופן כך וכך

blocks.text: *Chesed d'chachma*, the feeling that he is innocent, **also has ten**: **there's chesed and gevura of chesed d'chachma.** Letting him off because he is not really guilty, though he is no hero, is *gevura* of *chesed d'chachma*; saying he should not only go unpunished but be rewarded is *chesed* of *chesed d'chachma*.

phrases.en: even though you're going to say, well, wait a minute, but in *gevura* of *chachma*, whatever you're going to say is a merit, *gevura* of *chachma* is going to look at as a bad, negative point.
and any type of *chov* you're going to say is going to be turned into a merit by *chesed d'chachma*.

phrases.he: זהו כאשר הוא בעצם, בלתי התחלקות
phrases.en: That type of flipping only happens when you're in the *etzem midda*, which does not have *hischalkus* yet.

phrases.he: אבל בהתחלקות יוכל להיות גם בחסד שבחכמה בחינת דין ובדין שבחכמה בחינת חסד, כידוע)

blocks.text: The parenthesis raises an objection: whatever is a merit, **gevura of chachma is going to look at as a bad, negative point**, and the reverse in *chesed* of *chachma*. The same point can be read both ways.

blocks.title: The murderer's childhood
blocks.text:
A man convicted of murder pleads his childhood: a very bad environment, parents who traumatized him, so it is not really his fault. That merit comes from *chesed d'chachma*.

*Gevura* of *chachma* takes the same facts the other way: "That shows you that he's rotten to the core!" His moral framework was perverted from birth, there is no hope for him, throw the book at him. One point, both *zechus* and *chov*.

blocks.question: If *chesed* of *chachma* turns every point into a *zechus*, how can it still find a little *chov*?
blocks.text: **That type of flipping only happens when you're in the etzem midda, which does not have hischalkus yet.** Only the *etzem hamidda* (the essence of the attribute), before any *hischalkus* (division), turns every point over to its own side.

In *hischalkus*, though, there can be *din* in *chesed* of *chachma* and *chesed* in *din* of *chachma*. In the *etzem*, the *nekuda*, there is already a kind of division, like the *shochad* (bribe) of the *igulim* in chapter 17, but not a recognizable one: just a bias, turning everything to its side.

blocks.title: The bribed judge
blocks.text:
What connects to the *etzem hamidda* never compromises. A bribed judge will find the man innocent; but he was paid only to let him off, and whether the man also comes out a hero, "he wasn't paid for that." Outside the *etzem* he does as he likes.

That is *hispashtus* (spreading forth): the means, not the goal itself. In the means one can compromise, grant a point against the man and still hold him innocent.

So there are shades of *hiskalelus*. The parenthesis describes it in the *nekuda*, the *etzem midda*, where the little divisions are not a *hischalkus nikeres* (recognizable division), so we usually do not speak of them. This chapter is about the *hispashtus*: *sefira* and *partzuf* coming out of the *etzem nekuda*.

phrases.en: and similarly, that was in the *midda* of *chesed* of *chachma*, but the same would apply to the *middos* themselves, the actual feeling of love and the feeling of hate, for example.

phrases.he: החסד נחלק לי', כח''ב ומדות כו'
phrases.en: So the *chesed* itself divides into a *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* and *middos*,
even though that when you're judging you're not allowed to have mercy, there can be no mercy in judgment,
this is only in the essential *din*.
so too there's no *din* in *chesed atzmi*,
but when they spread out,
from the essence,

phrases.he: יש חסד בדין ודין בחסד כנזכר לעיל:

blocks.text: **The same would apply to the middos themselves, the actual feeling of love and the feeling of hate.** **The chesed itself divides into a Keser, chachma, bina and middos**: an intellect for the *chesed*, and emotions within it, *gevura* among them; and *din* has its own *sechel* (intellect) and *middos*.

*Ein merachamin badin*: **there can be no mercy in judgment**, so it seems love has no *din* either. But **this is only in the essential din.** The *etzem midda* has no *hiskalelus* of the opposite; its *hispashtus* allows combinations.

blocks.title: The judge and the first-time offense
blocks.text: A judge must judge objectively; tears cannot change the judgment. That is its *etzem*. But in how he judges, a first offense or other reasons may keep him from the maximum sentence: the law itself allows levels of guilt, the *middos* within it.
**So too there's no din in chesed atzmi**; **but when they spread out, from the essence**, there is *chesed* in *din* and *din* in *chesed*.

sections.title: The first kind: a thing nullified in its opposite, because the opposite is hidden in it
sections.summary: One kind of *hiskalelus* is *bittul* (nullification): the prosecutor becomes the defender, sugar overpowers cocoa, the merit itself becomes guilt. It is possible only because each side has its opposite hidden in it, as fire has something of water and *chesed* has a limit; without that, nothing would ever be included in its opposite.

phrases.he: והנה יש התכללות שנקרא ביטול דבר בהיפוכו המנגדו, והיה כמוהו ממש
phrases.en: There is one type of inclusion which is called the nullification of something in its opposite that opposes it, to the point where it becomes like it *mamash*, it becomes literally like it.
like the sweetening of severities in kindnesses
like the prosecutor gets transformed into a defender.
And also the opposite, when the defender gets turned over to a prosecutor.

blocks.text: Now come the types of *hiskalelus*. **There is one type of inclusion which is called the nullification of something in its opposite that opposes it, to the point where it becomes like it mamash**: totally turned over, **like the prosecutor gets transformed into a defender. And also the opposite.** When the person himself is won over it is even stronger: he was on the other side, so it lends strength.

blocks.title: The fighter against Chabad
blocks.text: Say a big fighter against *Chabad* admits it is true and becomes *Chabad*: that removes opposition and, since even he admits it, gives the defense a boost.

That is why a meeting of the *Alter Rebbe* with the Gra, the Vilna Gaon, would have been a big deal. Much of the opposition rested on the Gra, or was at least in his name. Had he met the *Alter Rebbe* and come out for it, much of the opposition would have dissolved.

phrases.en: or like the sweetening of bitter waters in sweet waters
or the opposite

blocks.title: Cocoa, coffee and sugar
blocks.text:
So too when a defender becomes a *mekatreg* (prosecutor). **Or like the sweetening of bitter waters in sweet waters**: cocoa is very bitter, but with a lot of sugar it just tastes sweet; so with coffee or lemonade.

**Or the opposite**: put a lot of bitter into something sweet and it tastes worse than plain bitter, because the contrast makes it stand out.

phrases.he: וכן ביטול שכל לזכות בשכל לחוב
phrases.en: and the same thing when an intellect for merit gets nullified in an intellect for guilt

blocks.text: **And the same thing when an intellect for merit gets nullified in an intellect for guilt**, as in the parenthesis: the merit, seen from *din*, itself becomes a *din*.

blocks.title: The murderer's childhood, turned over
blocks.text: The defense pleads the man's bad parents, friends and upbringing: anyone would have come to this, he is no worse than you. *Din* answers that such a start makes him bad through and through, a danger with no hope of reform; "we should throw the book at him." The merit itself becomes a *chov*.

blocks.title: Rochel buried by the road
blocks.text: The opposite way is the *sicha* (talk) about *Rochel Imeinu*. Yosef felt bad that his mother was not buried in the *Meoras HaMachpela*, and Yaakov's answer made it a *zechus*. Rochel's whole *inyan* was *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) for others; what she wanted was to give up her place there and lie by the road to *daven* for the Jews. Because she chose it, the loss brings out her main virtue.

phrases.en: This is a true inclusion.

phrases.he: והיינו רק לפי שיש כח זה במנגד עצמו
phrases.en: And the reason why this is possible is because there really is the other in the *menaged*, in the opposite side, there is hidden the other side also.

blocks.text: **This is a true inclusion**: one side loses its *metzius* (existence) and only the other is left. It is possible because **in the menaged, in the opposite side, there is hidden the other side also.**

Whoever opposes something has a little part of him that would go for it. Violent opposition shows he is scared of letting that side out. That does not make the thing right; it may really be bad. But someone who does not feel threatened does not feel drawn to it, and need not run from it so hard.

This is the difference between one who never sinned and a *baal teshuva*. The one who never sinned is supposed to say, "I want it, but what can I do? G-d told me not to." Never having tasted it, he thinks he is above it and looks down on those who do it. He must admit he would want it; once he thinks he does not, he is in trouble.

blocks.title: Adam thought he was a Rebbe
blocks.text: That was *Adam HaRishon*'s mistake. *Likkutei Dibburim* says he thought he was a Rebbe, above the bad and able to look at it and elevate it. But he had a *yetzer hara* (evil inclination) for it, still outside him since he had never tasted it, and looking at it drew him in.

But the Maggid says a *baal teshuva* should say, "I don't want it": he has tasted it, knows his desire, and needs a bigger guard. The *tzaddik* thinks he cannot enjoy it; the *baal teshuva* knows he can, and still must hate it and keep far from it, because he has the opposite side in him too.

phrases.en: and if it wasn't so, if it didn't have the opposite in it,
then it would not be able to be nullified and included within it.
For example, in something that's sweet, there is a hidden bitterness.
and in the bitterness there is a hidden sweetness.

phrases.he: כמשל ודמיון מבישול המרקחת מדבש וצנון,
phrases.en: Like we see in a *mashal* and a *dimyon* where you make a sauce, where you cook a sauce from honey and radishes, make a sweet and sour sauce.

phrases.he: שנעשה טעם עריבות, כולל מחריפות ומתיקות יחד
phrases.en: So, there you taste it's a delicious mixture of sharpness and sweetness together,
as is known.

blocks.text: **If it didn't have the opposite in it, then it would not be able to be nullified and included within it.** **In something that's sweet, there is a hidden bitterness**, or it could not turn bitter, **and in the bitterness there is a hidden sweetness.**

blocks.title: Honey and radish sauce
blocks.text: **You cook a sauce from honey and radishes**: **a delicious mixture of sharpness and sweetness together**, each bringing out the other. Add more of one and it tips: radish has some sweetness, and with enough sugar you taste only sweet; sugar has some bitterness, especially its aftertaste.

phrases.en: similarly,

phrases.he: יש מטבע האש במים וממים באש
phrases.en: There is something of the nature, the characteristics of fire within water, and something of the characteristics of water within fire.

phrases.he: על כן יתכלל אש במים או מים באש
phrases.en: Therefore, you can have a mixture where fire and water, or water from fire, will combine with each other.
like it says in *Sefer Yetzira*,

phrases.he: הוציא מים מאש ואש ממים כו'
phrases.en: Take out water from fire and fire from water,

blocks.text: **There is something of the nature, the characteristics of fire within water, and something of the characteristics of water within fire.** This is physical fire and water. The real *yesod* (element) of fire has no water in it, but physical fire and water are not the four *yesodos* themselves; everything physical is a mixture.

blocks.title: Lightning from clouds, water from rocket fuel
blocks.text: Lightning comes out of clouds of water, which can be ionized to bring out fire, as a flint does. And fire brings out water: burning oxygen and hydrogen makes water, so when the spaceship (he thinks it was Challenger) exploded on its way up, its rocket fuel left a cloud of water.

Water is wet and cold. Fire has some wetness, in that it holds together, and even a candle flame is only relatively hot. Water still has some warmth, not being frozen, and some dryness: its molecules keep some distance from each other.

**Therefore, you can have a mixture where fire and water, or water from fire, will combine with each other**, as *Sefer Yetzira* says: "**Take out water from fire and fire from water**," as burning produces water and lightning comes from water.

phrases.en: so too with the emotions of *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: מפני שיש דין בחסד וחסד בדין כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: because there's always included a certain *din* within *chesed* and a certain *chesed* within *din*.

phrases.he: יבוטל הדין בחסד או להיפוך החסד בדין
phrases.en: And therefore you can nullify the *din* in *chesed*, or the opposite, you can nullify the *chesed* within *din*.
and if it was not so, that there is the *chesed* in the *din*, and the *din* in the *chesed*,

phrases.he: לא היה מתכלל דבר בהיפוכו לעולם
phrases.en: Then it would never, one thing would never include within the other thing, they would never be able to unite and come together.

blocks.text: **So too with the emotions of chesed and gevura**, **because there's always included a certain din within chesed and a certain chesed within din.** First, *chesed* always has some limit: if you are nice to someone only so much or only in a certain way, there is *din* in it.

blocks.title: Your own child, and his enemy
blocks.text: You are kind to someone for what he did for you; were he to turn bad, the kindness would stop. Even unconditional love for your child is only because he is your child. And a *chesed* for one person is often a *din* for another: defend this one, and you have a *din* for his enemy.

So too there is *chesed* in *din*. A justice system is mainly there to punish, to stop people doing bad, and its premise is to uphold society for the people's good: "the main thing of the justice is a *chesed*." And whoever loves has, automatically, a *din* against what would destroy what he loves.

**Therefore you can nullify the din in chesed, or the opposite.** By the letter of the law something is bad, but fighting it would destroy everything you love, so the *din* gives way to the stronger *chesed*. Or being nice would destroy what you love, and you turn to *din*; or someone's kindness is outweighed by so many bad deeds.

**And if it was not so**, **one thing would never include within the other thing, they would never be able to unite and come together.**

That is the one type, where one thing is wholly *batel* (nullified) in the other: *hiskalelus* in the light itself. In *chachma* are *chesed* and *gevura*, and in those, *chesed* of *chesed* and *gevura* of *chesed*. The *bittul* can turn one into its opposite, or only temper it: innocent but no total *tzaddik* is *gevura* of *chesed*, still mainly *chesed*.

It is like *nekuda*, *sefira* and *partzuf*. In the *etzem hamidda*, a *nekuda*, everything is on one side: a bias that makes the case for innocence all *zechus*. Spread out as a *sefira*, it has shades within *chesed*: not totally good, yet better than anything else. The other side is granted and then *batel b'rov*, or in a thousand, or in sixty.

sections.title: The second kind, light in a vessel: kindness that is the strongest judgment
sections.summary: The next division is the lights going into vessels, where the opposite does not fight but strengthens. *Chesed sheb'gevura* is a judgment done by way of kindness: feeding your hungry enemy, the spy, the raise before the firing, G-d paying His enemies in this world, the voice that destroyed Sancheirev's camp. That is the strongest *din* of all.

phrases.he: אמנם הנה יש התכללות מדין בחסד מפני שהוא כמוהו בעצם,
phrases.en: There's another type of inclusion of *din* into *chesed* because they are inherently alike.
and not that it loses its nature.
Not only does it not oppose, not only does the *din* not oppose the *chesed* and need to be nullified by the *chesed*, but it actually helps the *chesed*, and it gives strength to the *chesed*.
and nevertheless,
It's still called *gevura* of *chesed*.
also the opposite,
there is also the idea of *chesed* of *gevura*,

blocks.text: Now a third type of *hiskalelus* (the first two fall under one category): *partzuf*, the *oros* (lights) coming into *kelim* (vessels), the light of *chesed* in the *kli* of *gevura*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The end of tape 83 announces the kind of hiskalelus that line 27 begins; tape 84 opens with it.

blocks.text: By the way, the *middos* counted in *Sefiras HaOmer* are those of *bina*. Unless it says otherwise, the first division into ten is within the lights and the next is the lights going into vessels: ten, then a hundred, *yud* and *yud* of *yud*. So each week is a *midda* in the light of *bina*, and each day that light in a vessel: *gevura* of *chesed* is the light of *chesed* of *bina* in the *kli* of *gevura*.

**There's another type of inclusion of din into chesed because they are inherently alike, and not that it loses its nature.** The *din* does not oppose the *chesed* and need to be nullified: **it actually helps the chesed, and it gives strength to the chesed**, **and nevertheless it's still called gevura of chesed.** **Also the opposite**: *chesed* of *gevura* strengthens the *gevura* and the *din*.

blocks.title: No compromise, unlike sugar in cocoa
blocks.text: Here one does not even temper the other. Sugar does overpower cocoa, but it is a fight, "and at the end of the day, chocolate is not as sweet as regular sugar": a compromise. Here there is none; the one strengthens the other.

phrases.en: and the *inyan* is, as is known,
like it says in the *passuk*,

phrases.he: אם רעב שונאך האכילהו לחם, כי גחלים כו'
phrases.en: It says, if your enemy is hungry, feed him bread, because it's like coals for his soul.

blocks.text: **The inyan is, as is known, like it says in the passuk**: "**If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread, because it's like coals for his soul.**" Sometimes the biggest *din* you can do to a person is to be nice to him. In plain *pshat*, having to take bread from you eats him up.

It also means your *yetzer hara*, hungry to be a *yesh*, to be bigger. Feed it the bread of Torah: promise to make it a big *metzius*, a rabbi, to teach it even *Chassidus*. It thinks it will be blown up big, but this destroys the *yetzer hara* and brings him to *teshuva*.

blocks.title: The spy
blocks.text: A spy acts friendly with the enemy, and that makes him the worst enemy: he gets close, learns all the secrets, "and then stab him in the back." The biggest *gevura*, though outwardly *chesed*.

This is the light of *chesed* in the *kli* of *gevura*, which is why they do not oppose each other. Lights of *chesed* and *gevura* are opposed, and *kelim* too; but the light of *chesed* in a *kli* of *gevura* is no contradiction, and in a way that *kli* is its most powerful, because there it is hidden.

blocks.title: The raise before the firing
blocks.text: Somebody he knew (he thinks it was an Iranian) said that an employer who really hated an employee would not simply fire him. First he gave him a raise and told him how much he is worth to the company. Once the man was used to the money and thought himself a bigger guy, they let him go as too great an asset to afford. Now he is never happy with less, and he finds work harder to get, since he thinks he is worth more. "So in a way, they totally ruined him."

sensitivity.reason: Presents a cruel workplace practice as what an Iranian said "they" would do, tying it to a nationality.
sensitivity.publishable: Somebody he knew said that an employer who really hated an employee would not simply fire him. First he gave him a raise and told him how much he is worth to the company. Once the man was used to the money and thought himself a bigger guy, they let him go as too great an asset to afford. Now he is never happy with less, and he finds work harder to get, since he thinks he is worth more. "So in a way, they totally ruined him."

phrases.he: הרי בחסד וטוב זה עושה לו רעה ודין גמור
phrases.en: So in this kindness and good that he's doing for him, he's really doing a complete evil to him and complete judgment, *din*, judgment on him,
to totally destroy his soul.
Similarly it says that G-d pays his enemies, he gives them their reward in this world so that he'll be able to totally destroy them in the next.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא כל בחינת דין ועונש שנעשה בבחינת חסד
phrases.en: and this is like the case with any *din* and *onesh*, any sort of judgment or punishment that is done in a way of *chesed*, that the *chesed* is the way that they're being punished,

phrases.he: הרי הוא עוז ותוקף הדין ביותר,
phrases.en: this is the strongest *din* possible.
and this is also called *chesed sheb'gevura*.

blocks.text: **In this kindness and good that he's doing for him, he's really doing a complete evil to him**, **to totally destroy his soul.** Were you mean to your starving enemy, he would be judged less harshly, since you are both mean; being nice leaves him the only bad one, and he is punished in full.

**Similarly it says that G-d pays his enemies**: their reward in this world, **so that he'll be able to totally destroy them in the next.** It looks like kindness, but it is total *din*: free to chase their bad things, they destroy themselves past repair.

blocks.title: Spoiling him to ruin him
blocks.text: One who hates his son does not rebuke him. Someone who really wanted to ruin a person, especially one a little rotten already, would spoil him with whatever he wants until he sank into bad habits, wholly incapacitated. That is the light of *gevura* in the *kli* of *chesed*: a *chesed* that is total *din*.

**Any din and onesh** (punishment) **that is done in a way of chesed** **is the strongest din possible, and this is also called chesed sheb'gevura.** The *chesed sheb'gevura* before was a compromise: one hates him, but less, since there is some good in him. Here it is the opposite, and stronger.

phrases.he: וכמו והשמיע יהו״ה את הוד קולו במחנה סנחרב
phrases.en: Like it says that *Hashem* made heard the glory of his voice in the camp of Sancheirev.

blocks.text: **Hashem made heard the glory of his voice in the camp of Sancheirev**: He killed them with a great *gilui Elokus* (revelation of G-dliness), a great *chesed*, and the verse uses *Havaya*, the name of *chesed*. The *gilui* was too great; they were *batel* and died. In a way it was the worst *din*: their whole being is to oppose G-d, and revealing that He alone is the true *metzius* destroyed theirs.

sections.title: Gevura sheb'chesed: harshness that is the strongest kindness
sections.summary: The opposite is kindness done in the garment of judgment: rain in measured drops, a teacher who brings it down, afflictions of love, tough love, the harsh cure that G-d prepared before the blow. That is stronger than plain kindness, and it is why our world is a *gevura* of *chesed*, a challenge to overcome.

phrases.en: and so too the opposite,
that the *gevura* of *chesed* is the strongest *chesed*.

phrases.he: שהמעשה של חסד עשוי במדת הדין
phrases.en: and this is when the act of kindness is done in a way through a means of *din*,
so that it'll be stronger.
like the severities of the, the *gevuros* of the rain,
So the rain comes in small drops, but the fact that the kindness is given out in little measured way, that is what allows a lot of rain to come.

blocks.text: **And so too the opposite**: **the gevura of chesed is the strongest chesed**, **when the act of kindness is done in a way through a means of din, so that it'll be stronger**, like **the gevuros of the rain**: it comes in small drops, and the kindness **given out in little measured way** **is what allows a lot of rain to come.**

blocks.title: Drizzle before the heavy rain
blocks.text: Rain that comes too fast floods. The ground first needs days of drizzle; moist, it can absorb the heavy rain that grows the plants. After a drought the ground is parched and hard, and even days of heavy rain just run off with the mud, a waste.

phrases.he: וכמו צמצום אור השפע בכל מקום, כדי שיתקבל
phrases.en: And this is like the *tzimtzum* of the light when something is being given over in any place, anytime that it's being given over, that's being made small so that it'll be able to be received.

blocks.text: **This is like the tzimtzum of the light** whenever something is given over: **made small so that it'll be able to be received.**

blocks.title: The teacher who brings it down
blocks.text: The more a teacher limits his intellect to bring it down to the student, the bigger the kindness. That is why you have a teacher; had you wanted it on his level, you could have read an advanced textbook.

phrases.en: And the same thing, the idea the division of the 72 bridges.
And the same thing with afflictions of love,
and like it says that a father that wants, that desires his son, that loves his son, he rebukes him.

blocks.title: The bridge with many arches
blocks.text: **The division of the 72 bridges** is the same. A bridge over a big river is a row of arches on pillars, like many small bridges joined, which slows and calms the water. So the light of *chesed* in a *kli* of *gevura* comes out small, divided and limited.

**Afflictions of love** too: G-d gives challenges to bring out a person's inner strength, or someone is harsh on another because he knows he has more potential. A father **that loves his son, he rebukes him.**

phrases.he: שהחסד נעשה בלבוש דמדת הדין דווקא
phrases.en: that there the kindness is done specifically through the garment of *din*.

phrases.he: והרי זה דווקא תוקף החסד יותר מעצם החסד
phrases.en: and this is really shows on a stronger kindness, and it's like a stronger love than the actual kindness itself.

blocks.text: **The kindness is done specifically through the garment of din**: total *chesed*, done tough and forceful for the other's good, like taking a knife from a child, a doctor's harsh treatments, any tough love.

This shows **a stronger love than the actual kindness itself.** Giving lollipops and presents is no big *chesed*. Immature kindness is really for yourself: you want to be seen as kind, so you do only what looks kind. Real love, caring for his good, is willing to be tough and outwardly mean, even if he thinks you mean.

phrases.en: like it says that G-d made the cure before the *makka*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב כי הוא יך וירפאנו
phrases.en: that G-d hits us, afflicts us, and heals us.
So if so, why did G-d make the problem?

phrases.he: אך על ידי הרפואה יברא ויתחזק יותר
phrases.en: but through being healed, then he becomes stronger.

phrases.he: כי החולה הוא בחינת הדין הקשה,
phrases.en: because the sickness is a harsh *din*, a harsh severity,

phrases.he: ויעובר על ידי מידת הדין שבחסד,
phrases.en: and it's taken away through the *din* of *chesed*, which is like harsh treatment,
That's healing through harsh things, the harsh medicines that are like dangerous to a healthy person, or different treatments and surgeries and things like that.

blocks.text: **G-d made the cure before the makka** (the blow): the cure is what He wants, since He loves us. **G-d hits us, afflicts us, and heals us.** **So if so, why did G-d make the problem**? **Through being healed, then he becomes stronger**: whatever does not kill you makes you stronger.
**The sickness is a harsh din**, **taken away through the din of chesed**: **healing through harsh things**, medicines that would endanger a healthy person, surgeries.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא בכל מיתוק הדין, בשרשו דווקא,
phrases.en: and this is the idea with the sweetening of *din*: it is always in its source,
which is the *din* of *chesed*.

phrases.he: להיותו תוקפו של חסד, לגבור על הדין ולהמתיקו כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **The sweetening of din: it is always in its source, which is the din of chesed**, the source of all *din*, and the strength of *chesed* is to overpower the *din*. G-d made bad things in the world as a challenge for us to overcome.

blocks.title: Basketball with an opponent
blocks.text: Practicing basketball alone is no great thing. Against an opponent it is much harder, so you enjoy it more: a bigger accomplishment, a bigger *chesed* when you score. The biggest *chesed* is the *din* of *chesed*, kindness that comes despite a challenge, so you want the opposition.

That is our world: *din* of *chesed*, a challenge to overcome through *avoda* (divine service). *Tohu* was like *chesed* of *chesed*; *Tikun* is *gevura* of *chesed*. We are in the second *shemita* of the first *yovel*: the first *yovel* is all *chesed*, its first *shemita* was *Tohu*, and the second, ours, is *gevura* of *chesed*.

So the world is dark, full of evil people who seem to succeed: a video game with a crowd of bad guys and one good guy who dodges every bullet and wins. The odds are way against us, and that is the great *chiddush*: we can still do it.

That is "*Zos chukas haTorah*." The *para aduma* makes one person pure by making another impure. Why must the *chesed* come through a *din*, even a *yerida l'tzorech aliya*? Because this is the one *chok*, the nature of our world; not only the decree, "*Shtok*, *kach ala b'ratzoni*," this is how I wanted it, and if you do not like it, too bad.

sections.title: Both at once: a light in a vessel is no contradiction
sections.summary: *Gevura sheb'chesed* and *chesed sheb'gevura* are the two greatest opposites, and yet they can come together, because each already shows two opposites: what it does and what it is inside. A light in a vessel is like matter and form, red ink spelling "green"; so Gavriel saved Avraham with fire, Avraham bound Yitzchak, and the Levi'im served the Kohanim.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן איכות אופני פרטי ההתכללות דחסד וגבורה,
phrases.en: So based on all this, it's understood the different ways that *chesed* and *gevura* can come together.
like *gevura* of *chesed*,
with, and that can unite with *chesed* of *gevura*,
even though they're two polar opposites seemingly, to their total opposites,

phrases.he: שזה תוקף החסד וזה תוקף בגבורה
phrases.en: that one is the forcefulness and the strength of *chesed*, the other one is the forcefulness and the strength of *gevura*,

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מצד התפשטות לבושים מחולפים,
phrases.en: and especially because of they switched, when you look at the garments which are switched,

phrases.he: שזה פועל דין וזה פועל חסד
phrases.en: that one is just when you look at the most external thing of what's going on, one is *din* and one is *chesed*.

blocks.text:
**So based on all this, it's understood the different ways that chesed and gevura can come together.** Dividing further in the light and in the vessel, even *gevura sheb'chesed*, the light of *chesed* in the *kli* of *gevura*, like a parent's love coming out as strictness, can **unite with chesed of gevura**, like the spy, whose hatred comes out as niceness.

This **even though they're two polar opposites seemingly**, **the forcefulness and the strength of chesed** against that **of gevura**, and especially when **the garments** **are switched**: outwardly the parent shows *din*, and the spy *chesed*.

phrases.en: nevertheless,

phrases.he: מצד שכל אחד פועל בשביל דבר היפוכו דוקא,
phrases.en: since each one is *poel* for the opposite,
that the *gevura* of *chesed*, which like a parent that is being strict and harsh with his son, the effect, the external thing is *din*, that he's being harsh,
but the real *pnimiyus*, the real intention is *chesed*, is kindness,
and the kindness within *gevura*, in other words the light of *gevura* going into the *kli* of *chesed*,
externally it's nice, it's being kind,
but the real thing inside of it is *din*, is harshness,

phrases.he: על כן יוכלו לבוא כאחד דוקא,
phrases.en: therefore they can come together at once

phrases.he: מפני שכל אחד מראה ב' הפכים על כל פנים
phrases.en: because each one has two opposites.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, since each one is poel** (works) **for the opposite**: in *gevura* of *chesed*, the strict parent, **the external thing is din**, but **the real intention is chesed**. In *chesed* of *gevura*, **externally it's nice**, but **the real thing inside of it is din.** **Therefore they can come together at once, because each one has two opposites.**

blocks.title: The teacher, from both sides
blocks.text: A teacher gives his students a *chesed* that comes from a *gevura*, limiting his *sechel*. For him it is the opposite: a *gevura*, limiting himself, that is really a *chesed*, being kind.
So whenever you face somebody, your right hand is on his left side, and your left on his right.

blocks.title: The spy who loves his country
blocks.text: The spy's niceness to the enemy is outward *chesed* meant to destroy them: for the enemy, *chesed* of *gevura*. But it is also *gevura* of *chesed*: out of love for his country he hides his true self and his patriotism and spends his time with the enemy, a big *gevura* for him. Which is it? Both, *davka* at once. What is *chesed* for one is *gevura* for the other, even in the outward effect: "in a way you always have them both together."

phrases.en: Like it says that Gavriel was sent that he saved Avraham.
and it says he cooled down the coals, that he made them not as hot,
So this is the idea of *gevura* of *chesed*,

blocks.title: Avraham in the furnace
blocks.text:
**Gavriel was sent that he saved Avraham.** When Avraham was thrown into the fiery furnace, the *malach* of *chesed* offered to bring rain or snow to put out the fire; Gavriel asked to save him, as being saved through *gevura* would be more of a *chiddush*. G-d said that since Avraham is one in the world He would save him Himself, and for wanting to, Gavriel later saved Chananya, Mishael and Azarya.

Perhaps it was still done through Gavriel, but two opposites at once show it came from G-d Himself: the fire killed the men who threw him in, "and at the same time, for him it was not hot."

Another time Gavriel was sent to pour coals on a town, and **he cooled down the coals**, not wanting just to destroy it. **So this is the idea of gevura of chesed**: saving Avraham, a *chesed*, through the fire, a *gevura*.

phrases.he: כמו זיעה טובה מוציא את חולי החום,
phrases.en: like a good sweat that takes out the sickness,
or like a medicine for some affliction, which is specifically like a harsh treatment.
and yet it says that Gavriel was the same one that hit *machane* Sancheirev,
which that is *chesed* of *gevura*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ויצא מלאך יהו״ה כו'
phrases.en: that he is called *malach Hashem*, a *malach* of kindness, because it was really the *chesed* of *gevura*.

blocks.text: **Like a good sweat that takes out the sickness**: sometimes it helps to wrap a sick person, even with a fever, to make him hotter so he sweats, and that takes away the fever. **Or like a medicine for some affliction, which is specifically like a harsh treatment.**

sensitivity.reason: Says that wrapping a sick person who has a fever to make him hotter helps take the fever away, which a reader could act on as medical advice.
sensitivity.publishable: **Like a good sweat that takes out the sickness**, **or like a medicine for some affliction, which is specifically like a harsh treatment.**
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Home treatment of a fever that a reader could try; weigh whether the line's own image (a good sweat) is enough, or his example can stand as a general remark rather than advice.

blocks.text: **Gavriel was the same one that hit machane Sancheirev**, **chesed of gevura**: **he is called malach Hashem, a malach of kindness**, severity through a great *gilui*. How? For Sancheirev it was *chesed* of *gevura*, but for the Jews a *gevura* against their enemy, so the *malach* of *gevura* could do it. A *malach* cannot do two opposite things, but this counts as one.

phrases.he: והיינו לאכללא שמאלא בימינא וימינא בשמאלא
phrases.en: This is what it means to include the left in the right and the right in the left.

phrases.he: שהוא כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה,
phrases.en: This is the idea, the light of *chesed* going into *kli hagevura*,
that the vessel does the opposite of its light.

phrases.he: שכלי הגבורה פועל דין, היפוך אור של חסד שבו
phrases.en: that the vessel of *gevura* affects *din* externally, which is the opposite of the light of *chesed* in it.

phrases.he: וכן להיפוך, כלי החסד פועל חסד, היפוך אור הגבורה שבו
phrases.en: In the same way, the vessel of kindness affects externally a kindness, which is the opposite of the light of *gevura* that is in it.

blocks.text: **This is what it means to include the left in the right and the right in the left**: the light of *chesed* in the *kli* of *gevura*, where **the vessel does the opposite of its light**, as a strict parent's *din* shows his love; and the reverse, **the vessel of kindness** outwardly kind with **the light of gevura** in it.

phrases.en: but this is really not an opposite at all,
because it's a light in the vessel,
which the idea of the light in the vessel is like a *chomer* and a *tzura*, the matter and the form.

blocks.text: **But this is really not an opposite at all, because it's a light in the vessel.** As long as it is good for him, you do not care which *kli* you use, whatever gets the job done. Light and vessel are **like a chomer and a tzura, the matter and the form**.

blocks.title: Red ink that spells "green"
blocks.text: Write "green" with a red pen: is it red or green? The ink is red, the form spells green, and there is no contradiction: one is *chomer*, the other *tzura*. So a vessel of *gevura* can be made a *chesed*, and the reverse, because "your goal and the means you use to accomplish the goal are totally independent."

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין התכללות דשם מ''ב ושם ע''ב,
phrases.en: as it is explained elsewhere about the inclusion of the name of 42 with the name of 72,

phrases.he: שהן ב' פרשיות דקריאת שמע כו'
phrases.en: which these are the two *parshiyos* of Shema.

blocks.text: **As it is explained elsewhere about the inclusion of the name of 42 with the name of 72, which these are the two parshiyos of Shema.** *V'ahavta* has 42 words. The name of 42 is that of *Ana B'choach*, whose initials make a 42-letter name: the name of *gevura*, *aliya* from below. *Ayin Beis*, 72, is the *gematria* of *chesed*.

He thinks this is not the famous *Shem Ayin Beis* of *chachma*, but another 72, a name of *chesed*, *hamshacha* (drawing down) from above. The first *parsha* opens with *V'ahavta*, *chesed*, a great *gilui* to a person on the level of a *tzaddik*; and that love brings the 42, a burning desire to go up to G-d, a *gevura*. So the two are together.

The second *parsha*, from *V'haya im shamoa* through *v'samtem*, has 72 words, the name of *chesed*, yet it warns of bad things if you do not listen. It speaks to a lower person, without that love or *gilui*: a *gevura*. But the challenge is there to bring out the *chesed*, and reveals a deeper one.

So each *parsha* is sometimes called the light of *chesed* in the *kli* of *gevura* and sometimes the reverse. The *Tzemach Tzedek* explains in *Derech Mitzvosecha*, *Shoresh Mitzvas HaTefilla*, that the *shem* (name) is a *memutza* between *or* and *kli*, and so is both.

phrases.he: וכמו עקידת יצחק באברהם, איש החסד
phrases.en: and similarly, like *Akeidas Yitzchak*, which was done by Avraham, which is *ish hachesed*.

blocks.text: **Like Akeidas Yitzchak, which was done by Avraham, which is ish hachesed** (the man of kindness). How could he be willing to sacrifice his son? His *chesed* is for G-d; whatever is G-dly is good to him, even through a *gevura*: "if G-d said to do it, then it's a *chesed*."

phrases.en: or like the Levi'im, when the Levi'im were given instead of the *bechorim* to help the Kohanim, so it says that they were waved, the Levi'im were waved, and they were given over to the Kohanim.
like it says that they will take them to you.
How can they serve the opposite?
and there's many examples of this.

blocks.text: **The Levi'im were given instead of the bechorim** (firstborn) **to help the Kohanim**, waved and **given over to the Kohanim.** But Kohanim are *chesed* and Levi'im *gevura*: **like it says** (*V'yilavu alecha*) **that they will take them to you**, so **how can they serve the opposite?** **And there's many examples of this.**

sections.title: Because each is divided, each finds its kind in the other
sections.summary: All this works only once each *sefira* is divided into its own ten, the level of *partzuf*: then each finds its kind in its opposite and wakes up, like milk that returns in meat. So Michael and Gavriel, fire and water, do not put each other out, and peace comes from separating the light, the goal, from the vessel, the means.

phrases.he: וכל זה אינו רק מצד בחינת ההתחלקות שבכל אחד
phrases.en: and the reason that this is possible is because once you have the level of *partzuf*, once there's a complete *hischalkus* in each and every one, each *sefira* already has its own ten, and divides into ten, and ten into ten.

phrases.he: על כן מצא מין את מינו וניעור,
phrases.en: So then each thing finds its *min*, and it gets woken back up.

phrases.he: גם בהיותם ב' הפכים ממש כו'
phrases.en: even though they're two opposites,

blocks.text: And **the reason that this is possible is because once you have the level of partzuf, once there's a complete hischalkus in each and every one**, each *sefira* has its own ten. So *matza min es mino v'nei'or*: **each thing finds its min** (its kind), **and it gets woken back up.**

blocks.title: Milk that wakes up in meat
blocks.text: This is a rule of mixtures, used also in *Eruvin*. A little milk in meat is *batel*; keep adding drops and eventually you taste the milk again, and it is not *batel* anymore: the *min* finds its *min*, wakes up and is a *metzius* again.

The Levi'im, outwardly *gevura*, have a little *chesed*, which the Kohanim bring out and use; and the Levi'im connect to the *gevura* in the Kohanim, which strengthens them. So each works with the other **even though they're two opposites**: once there is *hischalkus*, they can come together.

phrases.he: וכמו ענין התחלקות מיכאל וגבריאל, שר של אש ומים
phrases.en: like the divisions of Michael and Gavriel, which those are the angels of fire and water.

phrases.he: ואין מכבין זה את זה, כמו שכתוב עושה השלום כו'
phrases.en: nevertheless they do not extinguish each other, G-d makes peace *bimromav*, in the heavens he makes peace between *chesed* and *gevura*, between the *malachim* of *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: לפי שיש בכל אחד מהיפוכו המנגדו דוקא
phrases.en: since each one really has something of the opposite, so therefore they're able to come together.

blocks.text: **Michael and Gavriel**, **the angels of fire and water**, **do not extinguish each other**: *oseh shalom*, **G-d makes peace bimromav**, **between the malachim of chesed and gevura**, **since each one really has something of the opposite.**

blocks.title: Democracy
blocks.text: So in a democracy: in the light everyone's desires differ, but in action, the *kli*, they may find one thing each wants for his own reason, and then they can work together.

"*Oseh shalom bimromav, Hu ya'aseh shalom aleinu*": we ask the One who makes peace above to make it below, above all between G-d and the world. That needs a *birur* (clarification): separate the light from the vessel, the goal from the means. The goal is to connect to G-d; the physical world is the means. So first purify the goal.

Refine it until it is not *Gan Eden* or *Olam HaBa*, nor even being holy and close to Him, but simply doing whatever G-d says. Then ask how everything, spiritual and physical, serves that goal. *Tefillin* are good for a *mitzva*, but not on *Shabbos*, and in danger to life one does not run off to put them on. Once light and vessel are separated, they do not contradict: that is the source of peace.

Above there is already peace, because light and vessels are properly divided. With us it is not *mevorar*: we cannot tell what is the real *kavana* (intention), the *or*, and what only a *kli*. So we ask that it come down to us, and right after *oseh shalom* comes *yibaneh Beis HaMikdash*.

In the *Yehi ratzon* we ask for our portion in Torah, because Torah makes peace. The trouble is taking a thing called good as "one package deal," not seeing which part is good. The *or* is the real thing and the *kli* can change, because each has something of its opposite.

sections.title: The points cannot combine, except through mesirus nefesh, which turns even the essential bad to good
sections.summary: In the simple lights, the *nekudos* called *Kesarim*, nothing combines: the depth of good and the depth of bad have no connection. Yet the *baal teshuva*'s sins become merits, through *mesirus nefesh* that reaches the Essence above *chesed* and *gevura*; there prayer can change the way G-d does things. The three kinds become three ways of *avoda*: trust past the vessel, a light that overpowers, and enjoying the challenge itself.

phrases.en: but in the lights, the way they're completely simple,
which this is a level of the *nekudos*, even before *sefira*,
which are called the crowns, the *Keser* of each *sefira*,
they cannot unite at all.

phrases.he: מפני שכל אחד נבדל לגמרי מזולתו,
phrases.en: because each one is completely separate from the other one,

phrases.he: ולא ימצא בו כלל מבחינת המנגדו
phrases.en: and you have nothing of the opposite.

phrases.he: כמו עצם בחינת הטוב שבעצמיות נפש איש הטוב, הנקרא עומק טוב,
phrases.en: like the essence of the goodness in the inner self, the inner soul of a good person, which is called the depth of good, his pleasure in being good,
with the essence of bad,
which is called the depth of bad.

blocks.text: **But in the lights, the way they're completely simple**, **the nekudos, even before sefira** (the simple light is the *nekuda*; divided, the *sefira*; in a vessel, the *partzuf*), the *nekudos* **called the crowns**, **the Keser of each sefira**, **cannot unite at all**, **because each one is completely separate from the other one.**

It is **like the essence of the goodness in the inner self, the inner soul of a good person**, **the depth of good, his pleasure in being good**, **with the essence of bad**, **the depth of bad.** One enjoys good, the other bad, and there is no connection. One might use a bad person for something good, but at the level of the ultimate goal they cannot meet.

phrases.he: אך בבעלי תשובה אנו רואים שנהפך גם עצם הרע לטוב,
phrases.en: nevertheless, we do see a type of *hiskalelus*, this is the third type of *hiskalelus*, which is in the actual *etzem nekuda* itself, where the essence of the bad gets turned over to good.
And similarly, the sins themselves become merits.

phrases.he: הרי הוא מצד מסירת נפש בעצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: This is only possible when a person reveals their *mesirus nefesh*, their connection to G-d Himself,

phrases.he: שלמעלה גם מהתחלקות עצם החסד וגבורה
phrases.en: which is higher than the division of *chesed* and *gevura*.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, we do see a type of hiskalelus, this is the third type**, **in the actual etzem nekuda itself, where the essence of the bad gets turned over to good**: in the *baal teshuva*, whose **sins themselves become merits.** **This is only possible when a person reveals their mesirus nefesh, their connection to G-d Himself, which is higher than the division of chesed and gevura.**

There even the pleasure in rebelling against G-d and being one's own *metzius* reveals, at its depth, that there is only G-d, who can contract Himself so much that it looks like a real *metzius*: "a *gilui* of His power of *tzimtzum*." So G-d is revealed through the *aveiros* (sins) and the *mitzvos* equally.

*Lechatchila* it must be through the *mitzvos*, because G-d chose that the *giluyim* (revelations) matter. An *aveira* is bad only because a Jew is connected to G-d and G-d told him not to, so the feeling that it is bad reveals that connection, but in a negative way, which we do not want.
In the *etzem* both reveal G-d. Still a person must not do *aveiros*: "it's *mamash* a terrible thing." But once he has, he can do *teshuva* and reveal something good in it.

phrases.he: ולכך יכולים במסירת נפש דווקא, להתפלל ולומר יהי רצון, בעצם, מלפניך כו'
phrases.en: And this is why specifically when a person has *mesirus nefesh* can they *daven* and ask G-d to change the way He does things.

blocks.text: **This is why specifically when a person has mesirus nefesh can they daven and ask G-d to change the way He does things.** The secret of being answered in *Shemoneh Esreh* is the *mesirus nefesh* of *Krias Shema* before it: it reveals an *etzem* connection where *chesed* and *gevura* are one, and there He too, as it were, has *mesirus nefesh* to do it your way.

phrases.he: וכן ויעבור יהו״ה על פניו כו'
phrases.en: and this is also like it says that G-d passed over his face, in other words went past the *pnimiyus*, which is like the reason of the *sechel*.

phrases.he: להפוך גם הדין בעצם לחסד כו',
phrases.en: to turn even the essential *din* into a *chesed*,

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בענין י''ג תקוני דיקנא כו' ודי למבין
phrases.en: as it's explained about the 13 parts of the beard.

blocks.text: So too **G-d passed over his face**, **went past the pnimiyus, which is like the reason of the sechel**, and said the thirteen *middos harachamim* (attributes of mercy), **to turn even the essential din into a chesed**: forgiving sins, turning *zedonos* (willful sins) into *zechuyos* (merits). That is possible when we connect to G-d above *sechel* and above Torah.

blocks.title: Erase me from Your book
blocks.text: Moshe said, "If You're not going to forgive them, *mecheini na*, erase me from Your book": the Rebbe explains he meant to go above the Torah. G-d answered, "The one that sins against Me, I will erase from My book": He prefers people to keep the rules, and one who will not, He forgives above them.

phrases.he: (והיינו על ידי בחינת הקו וחוט, שיש בו מכח עצמות אור אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: This is coming from the *Kav* and *chut*, which has in it the *koach* of G-d himself.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב זכרונם לברכה אליו ולא למדותיו,
phrases.en: like our Sages taught us, we should pray to G-d and not to his *middos*.
and not even to his essential *middos*,

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם ודי למבין):
phrases.en: like will be explained with the help of G-d, and this is sufficient for the understanding.

blocks.text: As explained about the thirteen *tikunei dikna*, the parts of the beard (chapter 25, *im yirtzeh Hashem*). **This is coming from the Kav and chut, which has in it the koach of G-d himself**: like the teacher who sets up the class, "since he makes the rules, he can break the rules."
*Eilav v'lo l'middosav*: **we should pray to G-d and not to his middos, and not even to his essential middos**, as will be explained.

From here, or a little before, and for much of the rest of the book, he does not clearly separate *mashal* from *nimshal*, and you have to work harder to *chap* (catch) the point. The point of the three levels: G-d can reveal any *or* through any *kli*, so we must tell the *or* from the *kli*. The five chapters on *oros* and *kelim* later make it clearer.

One *avoda* is *emuna*: trusting that whatever G-d does is for the best, that He loves you. The vessel may look like *gevura*, but it is really *chesed*, so you are always happy and never worried. Something that looks good can bring bad, and the reverse; how it looks "is totally irrelevant." Do not panic when it starts to look bad, nor exult when it looks good.

So everything is in G-d's hands. He gives us some *bechira* (free choice), but all we do is only a vessel, which He can fill with whatever He wants. No business deal is a foolproof *kli*; there is no *kli* He cannot turn over. So you need *emuna*, trust, and His *bracha*, without which your vessel is meaningless and can turn to the opposite.

Another *hiskalelus* is in the *or* itself. Within *kedusha* (holiness) some things reveal G-d more and some less, and the *or* of *kedusha* must grow strong enough to overpower the other side: a person's desire for bad wholly overpowered by his pleasure in good. In the first way, light and vessel, what seems to oppose G-d is irrelevant: *bittul hayesh*, keeping its *metzius* and *batel*.

This is in a way a higher *bittul*: G-d's *gilui* is so great that *kula kamei k'lo chashiv*, and any opposition is blown away, as for the *tzaddik*. One may say the bad still hurts; but the little pain of this world is nothing beside the good of doing *mitzvos* and connecting to G-d, "a tiny nothing." It is there, yet as if *batel*.

Higher still, in the *etzem or*, is the third *hiskalelus*, the *gilui hayechida* (essence of the soul), where the bad itself becomes good. His *mesirus nefesh* is such that suffering for G-d is not merely worth it: he enjoys it, as another way of expressing his connection. That is *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him).

blocks.title: Playing the game
blocks.text: One who knows he is playing a game does not feel he is enduring pain to get something good: he chooses it and enjoys the challenge. That is "redeem my soul in peace from those that fight with me": something fights him, *mikrav li*, and still it is *pada v'shalom*. When the *yechida* is revealed, the opposition is there only to challenge you, part of your *avoda* and your own *metzius*.

In a way this is like the first, which is why *Tikun*, the *or* in the *kli*, is higher than *Tohu*, *hiskalelus* only in the *or*. But the first still sees the thing as bad, a means to something good; here, even as an end in itself, you enjoy the way you do it.

blocks.title: Winning the game or playing it
blocks.text: Do you enjoy winning the basketball game, or playing it? If only winning, the opponent is a frustration. With a more mature appreciation you enjoy the challenge itself while you are in it, and the difficulty becomes a good thing.

Even if he cannot feel it, a person can know that from G-d's point of view, creating the world from nothing, it is like a game or story where nothing is a means to an end. G-d did not want only the *aliya*, with the *yerida* merely for its sake; He could have made the *aliya* without it. "Rather, we must say that G-d enjoys the *yerida* itself."

Seen that way, the whole goal of a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below) and *Moshiach* was for us to have the challenge of the *avoda*; when *Moshiach* comes we will yearn for the *avoda* of *galus*. Knowing this, even without feeling it, helps a person overcome and be happy now.

So *Tanya* says a *beinoni* should be very happy even if he never wholly overcomes his *yetzer hara*. There is a virtue in being a *tzaddik*, but also in the struggle, "and in a way, G-d likes that better." May we have the complete *bittul* of the *etzem hara*, turned to good, *v'es ruach hatumah a'avir min ha'aretz*, with *Moshiach* right away.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does a bribed judge show the difference between the *etzem hamidda* and its *hispashtus*?
Why can a thing be nullified in its opposite only if the opposite is already hidden in it? Give his examples from food and from fire and water.
Why is feeding your hungry enemy, or G-d rewarding the wicked in this world, the strongest *din* of all?
What makes tough love a stronger *chesed* than giving lollipops and presents?
How can *gevura sheb'chesed* and *chesed sheb'gevura* come together, and what does the red pen that writes "green" show about a light in a vessel?
Why can the depth of good and the depth of bad not be included in each other, and how does *mesirus nefesh* turn even the sins of a *baal teshuva* into merits?

notes.text: Line 74: the transcript has him read "ולכך יכולים במסירת נפש דוקא לפעול שינוי רצון בעצם" (87 w2004-2013) where the chapter has "להתפלל ולומר יהי רצון, בעצם, מלפניך". His English right after (87 w2014-2037), "can they daven and ask G-d to change the way He does things", renders the chapter's words (להתפלל ולומר יהי רצון), so the transcript's Hebrew is probably the machine's mishearing. The phrase keeps the chapter's Hebrew and cites that English; a reviewer may listen.

The spy: in tape 84 (w838-853) he calls the spy's friendliness the light of chesed in the kli of gevura, and spoiling someone to ruin him the light of gevura in the kli of chesed (84 w1471-1484). In tape 86 (w80-155, w345-370) gevura sheb'chesed is the light of chesed in the kli of gevura (the strict parent) and chesed sheb'gevura, the spy, is the light of gevura in the kli of chesed, which reverses the first statement about the spy. Both are kept as he said them.

Phrases that cite his explanation a sentence or two after the reading rather than a word-for-word rendering: line 6 (81 w743-768), the second half of line 19 (82 w1034-1061), the second half of line 36 (85 w70-99), line 61 (87 w114-159) and line 64 (87 w219-265, tidied). Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: line 3, the end of line 7, line 9, the end of line 13, the end of line 18, the end of line 29, "Kel rachum" in line 75, and line 45.

Sources as he gave them, unchecked: a sicha on Rochel and Yosef's "yesh b'libcha alai" (82 w781-969); Likkutei Dibburim on Adam HaRishon thinking he was a Rebbe (82 w1359-1405); "the Maggid" on what a baal teshuva should say (82 w1468-1503); the Tzemach Tzedek in Derech Mitzvosecha, Shoresh Mitzvas HaTefilla (86 w2311-2350). The angel who offered to put out Avraham's furnace with rain or snow he calls "the malach of chesed" (86 w893-939); in Pesachim 118a it is Yurkemo, the angel of hail. The "different time" Gavriel cooled the coals (86 w1087-1141) he does not name; a reviewer may compare Yoma 77a.

Counts he gives from memory: 42 words in the first parsha of Shema and 72 in the second, from V'haya im shamoa until v'samtem (86 w1875-1890, w2098-2116); 42 words in Ana B'choach whose initials make the 42-letter name. He says himself that he does not think the Shem Ayin Beis here is the famous one of chachma (86 w1957-1996). Kept as said; a reviewer may count.

"Which one, was it Challenger" (83 w503-563): he is unsure which spacecraft he means; kept with his doubt. The tape says we are in the second shemita of the first yovel and that Tohu was the first (85 w1415-1478); kept as said.

Sensitivity: the raise-before-the-firing story is flagged (other-groups) because he attributes the practice to an Iranian and "they"; the good sweat for a fever is flagged (health-or-legal) because it reads as advice. Left unflagged on purpose: the fighter against Chabad and the hypothetical meeting of the Alter Rebbe with the Gra (82 w184-363), a historical remark that criticises no one; the justice system as mainly punishment (83 w1188-1252) and the democracy mashal (87 w619-698), which take no side; the murderer with a bad childhood (81, 82), an example made up for the point. The Alter Rebbe and the Gra aside (82 w275-363) was reconsidered in review and left unflagged: it names the Gra only to say the opposition was based on him, or used his name even if it was not really from him, and criticises neither. The fever block's publishable text keeps only his two images (the good sweat, the harsh medicine) without the instruction.

82 w364-377 ("the same thing, the opposite, when a defender becomes a mekatreg") is said before he reads line 17 and closes line 16; it is the first sentence of the cocoa block under line 17. 83 w1993-2051 announces the kind of hiskalelus that line 27 begins and is placed there with outOfPlace.
All eight tapes have Sofer's word times, not re-timed ones: the seconds can be off; the word ranges are right.
